speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is causing these symptoms, have you been feeling unusually tired, or do you notice that your gums bleed easily when you brush?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the combination of gum bleeding, frequent nosebleeds, and petechiae on the extremities is very concerning. To narrow this down, has the child had any other injuries or been on any medications recently? Also, do the bruises appear spontaneously without any clear trauma?

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work results indicate normal platelet counts and normal clotting times, which makes thrombocytopenia or a primary coagulation factor deficiency unlikely. Given the child's age and the specific pattern of mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae, have you noticed any family members with similar bleeding issues, and have you noticed the bleeding seems to stop spontaneously without pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu Syndrome)

The normal platelet count and coagulation profile rule out thrombocytopenia and clotting factor deficiencies, pointing instead to a vascular structural abnormality. Given your history of spontaneous mucous membrane bleeding, nosebleeds, and petechiae, do you have a family history of similar bleeding disorders, and do you notice small, dilated blood vessels on your lips, tongue, or fingers?
